results.title: Fatal US Apache crash puts spotlight on the attack helicopter's safety record
results.description: #AH64Apache #ApacheHelicopter #AttackHelicopter #USArmy #indianarmy Fatal US Apache crash puts spotlight on the attack helicopter's safety recordThe AH‐64 Apache is regarded as the world’s premier attack helicopter, combining advanced sensors, precision weapons, and unmatched battlefield versatility. First deployed in Panama in 1989 and later spearheading the Gulf War air campaign, Apaches destroyed nearly 300 Iraqi tanks and radar sites, cementing their reputation. Operated by 19 nations, including India, the helicopter has proven itself in diverse environments, from rainforests to the Himalayas during the Galwan standoff. Armed with Hellfire and Spike missiles, and now integrating loitering munitions, the Apache continues to expand its lethal arsenal. However, its combat success is offset by a troubling safety record. Since 1980, 193 crashes have claimed nearly 120 lives, with the latest incident in Texas killing two pilots. U.S. Army data shows Apaches suffer 4.41 Class‐A mishaps per 100,000 flight hours, far higher than Black Hawks.
